key.name: panel-position
key.description: Which panel box the indicator is placed in. One of: left, center, right.

key.name: hide-native-activities-dots
key.description: GNOME Shell 46's Activities button (top-left) renders small workspace dots and clicking it toggles the Activities overview. When true, this extension hides the whole button; its roles move to the extension's own indicator -- clicking the area around the workspace squares toggles the overview, and scrolling over the indicator switches workspaces. The dots are additionally collapsed via a scoped CSS override on an internal, undocumented style class ("workspace-dot") as a defensive layer. Turn this off if it stops working correctly on a future GNOME version, or if you want both indicators visible.

key.name: square-size
key.description: Width and height, in pixels, of each workspace square.

key.name: square-spacing
key.description: Horizontal gap, in pixels, between adjacent workspace squares.

key.name: square-border-radius
key.description: Corner radius, in pixels, of each workspace square.

key.name: square-padding
key.description: Internal padding, in pixels, between a square's border and its label.

key.name: font-size
key.description: Font size, in points, of the workspace number label.

key.name: font-weight
key.description: CSS font-weight of the workspace number label. One of: normal, bold, 600.

key.name: indicator-style
key.description: Visual style of the squares. One of: filled, outline.

key.name: label-style
key.description: How each workspace square is labeled. One of: numbers (1 2 3), roman (I II III), devanagari (१ २ ३), letters (A B C), letters-lower (a b c), devanagari-letters (क ख ग), dots (●). Unrecognized values fall back to numbers.

key.name: active-background-color
key.description: Hex color (e.g. #3584e4) for the active workspace square. Empty string uses the current GNOME theme accent color.

key.name: inactive-background-color
key.description: Hex color for inactive workspace squares. Empty string uses the current GNOME theme default.

key.name: active-text-color
key.description: Hex color for the label text of the active workspace square. Empty string uses the current GNOME theme default.

key.name: inactive-text-color
key.description: Hex color for the label text of inactive workspace squares. Empty string uses the current GNOME theme default.

key.name: panel-autohide
key.description: Slide the GNOME top panel off-screen like a dock, reclaiming its space for windows. It slides back in while the pointer touches the top edge, when the reveal keybinding (default Super+Z, see panel-reveal-toggle) toggles it open, in the Activities overview, while a panel menu is open, and while the current workspace is empty. The panel itself is not restyled, only hidden and revealed.

key.name: panel-slide-time
key.description: How long, in milliseconds, the auto-hidden panel takes to slide in or out. The same duration is used in both directions.

key.name: panel-opacity
key.description: Opacity of the top panel's background, in percent. 100 keeps the theme's normal solid background untouched; lower values make it translucent, 0 fully transparent. Panel text and icons are unaffected. Independent of auto-hide.

key.name: enable-quick-menu
key.summary: Show the Tessera quick menu in the top panel
key.description: Adds a Tessera button to the right side of the top panel. Its popup is organised into Overview / Tools / Keys tabs: quick toggles (tiling, focus border, panel auto-hide) and gap steppers, quick tools (a port killer and a screen color picker) with their recent history, and a read-only reference of every configured keybinding. Off by default; the extension's other features work regardless of this setting.

key.name: picked-colors
key.description: History of the most recent colors chosen with the color picker, newest first, as #RRGGBB hex strings. Capped at 20 entries. Shown in the quick menu's Tools tab; safe to clear.

key.name: killed-ports
key.description: History of the most recent ports acted on with the port killer, newest first, as short display strings (port number, optionally with the process name). Capped at 20 entries. Shown in the quick menu's Tools tab; safe to clear.

key.name: enable-tiling
key.description: Hyprland-style dynamic tiling: normal application windows are automatically arranged in a dwindle (binary split) layout per workspace and monitor. Dialogs, utility windows, minimized and user-maximized windows float. When disabled, windows keep whatever geometry they last had and are never repositioned.

key.name: tiling-gap-inner
key.description: Gap, in pixels, between adjacent tiled windows.

key.name: tiling-gap-outer
key.description: Gap, in pixels, between tiled windows and the edge of the monitor work area.

key.name: floating-window-size
key.description: When a window is popped out to float (the toggle-floating keybinding), it is centered on its monitor's work area at this percentage of the work area's width and height. It can then be freely moved and resized -- the tiler never repositions a floating window; it only keeps it stacked above the tiled ones.

key.name: new-window-new-workspace
key.summary: Open every new window on a workspace of its own
key.description: When on, a newly opened top-level application window is moved onto a fresh workspace and the view follows it there, so each app gets a workspace to itself. Dialogs, popups, transient and sticky windows are never moved. A window that opens onto an otherwise empty workspace is left where it is -- it already has that workspace to itself. Where the fresh workspace comes from is controlled by new-window-adjacent-workspace. Requires dynamic workspaces (GNOME's default) to actually create workspaces; with static workspaces it degrades to moving the window to the existing workspace in that position.

key.name: new-window-adjacent-workspace
key.summary: Put that new workspace right next to the current one
key.description: Only meaningful while new-window-new-workspace is on (ignored otherwise). When off, a new window goes to the trailing workspace at the end of the strip -- the empty one GNOME always keeps there -- so the workspace order stays chronological. When on, a brand-new workspace is instead inserted immediately to the right of the window's current workspace, shifting every later workspace along, so related work stays adjacent. Either way the view follows the window onto its new workspace.

key.name: enable-focus-border
key.description: Hyprland-style border drawn around the currently focused window, on every workspace and monitor, independent of tiling (floating windows get one too).

key.name: focus-border-color
key.description: Hex color (e.g. #3584e4) for the focus border. Empty string uses the current GNOME theme accent color, the same logic as the active workspace square.

key.name: focus-border-width
key.description: Thickness, in pixels, of the focus border.

key.name: focus-border-radius
key.description: Corner radius, in pixels, of the focus border, applied uniformly to every window.

key.name: enable-custom-keybindings
key.description: Master switch for the extension's workspace-switching keybindings. When disabled, no default GNOME keybindings are modified.

key.name: workspace-jump-last
key.description: Switch to the last workspace on the strip. With dynamic workspaces (GNOME's default) that is always the empty one GNOME keeps at the end, so this is "go to a blank workspace" regardless of how many exist.

key.name: window-move-last
key.summary: Move focused window to the trailing workspace
key.description: Move the focused window to the last workspace on the strip and follow it there. With dynamic workspaces that workspace is always empty, so this is the "give this window a fresh workspace at the end" counterpart to the insert-left/insert-right bindings.

key.name: workspace-swap-1
key.summary: Swap current workspace contents with workspace 1

key.name: workspace-swap-2
key.summary: Swap current workspace contents with workspace 2

key.name: workspace-swap-3
key.summary: Swap current workspace contents with workspace 3

key.name: workspace-swap-4
key.summary: Swap current workspace contents with workspace 4

key.name: workspace-swap-5
key.summary: Swap current workspace contents with workspace 5

key.name: workspace-swap-6
key.summary: Swap current workspace contents with workspace 6

key.name: workspace-swap-7
key.summary: Swap current workspace contents with workspace 7

key.name: workspace-swap-8
key.summary: Swap current workspace contents with workspace 8

key.name: workspace-swap-9
key.summary: Swap current workspace contents with workspace 9
key.description: Swap all movable windows between the current workspace and workspace N, then follow the content to N. No-op if the current workspace is empty or N is the current/out-of-range workspace; if N is empty the windows just move there and the emptied current workspace is culled (dynamic workspaces).

key.name: window-move-new-left
key.summary: Move focused window to a new workspace inserted to the left

key.name: window-move-new-right
key.summary: Move focused window to a new workspace inserted to the right

key.name: layout-toggle-stacked
key.summary: Toggle stacked layout on the current workspace

key.name: window-toggle-floating
key.summary: Toggle floating for the focused window

key.name: window-toggle-maximize
key.summary: Toggle maximize for the focused window
key.description: Maximize the focused window to fill the work area (keeping the top panel and title bar, like the window's maximize button), or restore it if already maximized.

key.name: window-toggle-fullscreen
key.summary: Toggle fullscreen for the focused window
key.description: Put the focused window into true fullscreen (covering the whole monitor, including the top panel), or leave fullscreen if already in it. While a window fullscreened this way is focused, Escape leaves fullscreen; opening a new application window also leaves it.

key.name: tool-port-killer
key.description: Opens the port-killer dialog (type a TCP port, SIGTERM whatever is listening on it). Also reachable from the quick menu's Tools tab. Independent of the quick menu setting.

key.name: tool-color-picker
key.description: Starts the screen color picker (click a pixel to copy its #RRGGBB hex to the clipboard). Also reachable from the quick menu's Tools tab. Independent of the quick menu setting.

key.name: panel-reveal-toggle
key.description: Toggles the auto-hidden top panel open (and closed again). Only active while "Auto-hide the top panel" is on; it latches the panel visible until pressed again, then the normal reveal conditions (pointer at the top edge, overview, etc.) resume. Has no effect when auto-hide is off.

key.name: window-fullscreen-escape
key.summary: Leave fullscreen (internal, active only while a keybind-fullscreened window is focused)
key.description: Accelerator grabbed dynamically by the extension ONLY while a window it fullscreened via window-toggle-fullscreen is focused, so Escape leaves that fullscreen. Not a general shortcut: it is un-grabbed the instant such a window is no longer focused, so it never intercepts Escape from ordinary windows. Change it if Escape conflicts with how you use fullscreened apps.
